term_glossary.tooltip: A defined reference used to locate or orient a feature in a drawing or assembly.
Reserved space that must remain clear for a defined connection, movement, access or service function.
OpenU (OU): the 48 mm vertical equipment pitch described for Open Rack; it is distinct from the 44.45 mm EIA rack unit.
Conventional EIA rack-unit spacing of 44.45 mm; do not substitute its count for an OpenU count.
A conductive distribution assembly with defined current-carrying and connection interfaces. Its supported rating depends on the design and conditions.
A connection made without direct access to the mating interface; defined alignment and operating conditions still apply.
Protective connection of relevant conductive parts; it must not be confused with the operating DC return circuit.
The protective earthing function in the cited design, distinct from the normal operating DC return.
The return path of the operating DC power circuit. Its relation to chassis or earth follows the qualified design.
Coolant distribution unit: equipment that manages the technology-side cooling interface; functions and loop separation depend on the design.
An assembly that distributes or collects coolant among the branches of a defined cooling arrangement.
One additional unit beyond the units needed for the stated capacity requirement. It does not establish independence across every shared path.
Power supply unit: a conversion module whose output and fault behavior are qualified within its specified conditions.
Power monitoring module: the specified monitoring and management interface for the selected shelf implementation; it is not a substitute for local protection.
A portion of a system whose shared dependency can cause its members to be affected together by a failure.
The circuitry and control at equipment input that govern accepting and disconnecting supplied power under the applicable requirements.
An energy-storage function used to supply or absorb power for defined events, subject to power, energy, state and operating limits.
Coordinated allocation or redistribution of power within an architecture; it does not create capacity beyond the available system.
Reducing demand variation presented at a defined boundary, while maintaining the limits of the load and any buffering system.
A rack-adjacent assembly that relocates defined power functions; its input, output, capacity and interfaces depend on the design.
The location where power conversion changes the electrical interface. Upstream voltage changes do not automatically change an unchanged downstream bus.
Open Rack Wide: a shared interface specification for a wider rack platform; implementation documents define external dimensions and payload choices.
High-power rack architecture. Ratings and distribution arrangements must remain tied to the selected implementation and revision.
Equipment load carried by the rack, distinguished from the rack frame's own mass; qualified configuration and distribution conditions matter.
An internal equipment-supporting assembly in a specific implementation, not a guarantee of a universal ORW arrangement.
Pivoting Blind Mate Coupling: specified plug and socket interfaces and performance requirements for a pivoting blind-mate fluid connection.
The defined distance relationship between the coupling's specified reference planes in a mated condition.
Departure from the specified alignment relationship; permitted offset, angle and combined conditions follow the applicable interface requirements.
Technology cooling system: the equipment-side cooling system in the illustrated CDU-separated arrangement.
Facility water system: the receiving facility-side water circuit in the illustrated separated-loop arrangement.
The resistance a configured flow path presents to coolant flow; equipment, hoses, couplings and manifolds contribute.
The controlled verification and acceptance process that establishes readiness of a configured installation for specified operating conditions.
The space needed for the approved access, isolation, removal or replacement activity, including required movement.
A concentrated load at a support or contact location, such as a wheel or foot; total rack mass alone does not establish local suitability.
Evidence that a stated design or configuration meets defined conditions and acceptance criteria; applicability depends on the tested scope.

lms_catalog.short_description: Connect Open Rack architecture, ORv3, high-power systems and ORW to practical power, cooling and deployment reviews.
lms_catalog.overview: Explore Open Rack as a connected system of mechanical, electrical, cooling and operational interfaces. This seven-module course develops an engineering approach to reviewing ORv3, high-power racks and Open Rack Wide, using specification-based diagrams, narrated teaching animations, expert walkthroughs and applied design decisions. Learn to compare implementations, identify missing evidence and plan a supported deployment. Key specifications, an integrated glossary and related OCP Academy courses provide paths to deeper study.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Includes all embedded recordings, slide narration, figures, design-review cases and knowledge checks. Linked external courses and Summit recordings are optional additional study.

modules.summary: Establish the rack's role in the open ecosystem, distinguish specifications from implementations, and define the workload and deployment envelope before selecting equipment.
Trace ORv3 frame datums, OpenU and RU grids, power delivery, bonding, cooling and service access. Review whether equipment interfaces agree across a configured rack.
Compare implementations and supplier evidence, use Marketplace and contribution resources appropriately, and plan compatibility, transport, site-route and acceptance reviews.
Evaluate high-power rack architecture, usable capacity, power management, buffers, fault domains and recovery. Recalculate the workload budget when a supply path is lost.

Compare sidecars, higher-voltage distribution and conversion boundaries across the complete power path. Connect changing AI workload demand to buffering, sharing and rack-to-facility responsibilities.
Review ORW base and implementation specifications, frame and canister interfaces, configured payload, lifting, transport, routing and facility integration.

Follow the complete cooling loop and PBMC interface, assess flow, pressure, residual air heat and serviceability, and assemble commissioning and handover evidence for an integrated rack design review.
